function: Device activity detection (which IoT devices are active) for grant-free massive random access, using unfolded projected gradient descent with a mixture-of-experts gate (p. 3).
system: Single-cell uplink: BS with M=32 antennas, reflecting IRS with N=40 elements, K=100 devices (activity probability 0.2); frequency band not stated (pp. 1, 4).
method: Deep-unfolded projected gradient descent (4 layers) with MLP gate choosing one of three covariance experts; end-to-end incremental training, gate supervised by KL loss to true group proportions (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Self-generated Rician (kappa 10 dB) and Rayleigh fading, three-dimensional BS/IRS/device layout, large-scale fading -60-22log10(distance product) dB; no standard channel model or dataset named (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Training conditions not described beyond incremental training [16]; tests at kappa=10 dB, noise -95 dBm, 40/30/30% device groups (Fig. 3) and K1 share 0-80% (Fig. 4) (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: coordinate descent (CD), derived PGD (with and without group knowledge). Learned: two deep-unfolding detectors [19], [20] and transformer detector [21] (p. 4).
metrics: Probability of false alarm P_F and missed detection P_M (P_M-P_F curves, error rate P_F=P_M), inference latency in ms (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Order O(I(M^3+LM)) without MoE and O(LM+I(M^3+LM)) with MoE (I=4, M=32, L=20); measured inference latency in ms, Fig. 5 (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "devices in K2 following Rician fading and those in K3 following Rayleigh fading". Custom simulator with Rician and Rayleigh fading and its own large-scale model (p. 4); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 5: "Fig. 4 illustrates the flexibility and generalization" ability, with the K1 share swept from 0% to 80%; but the paper never states which shares were used in training (p. 4: "we use incremental training [16]" only), so unseen conditions are not stated, and a parameter sweep alone does not count.
q3_support: p. 4: "two deep unfolding baselines [19], [20], traditional coordinate descent (CD) algorithm", plus the derived PGD and a transformer-based detector [21]; all compared on P_M and P_F in Fig. 3 (p. 4).
q4_support: p. 4: "The computational complexity of the deep unfolding network without the MoE module is" O(I(M^3+LM)), and O(LM+I(M^3+LM)) with the MoE module; p. 5: "the shortest inference time among three deep learning methods" (Fig. 5 latency in ms).
q5_support: p. 4: "set the locations of the BS and the IRS at (0, 0, 10) and (5, 50, 10) in meter" defines a self-generated simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and names no public dataset.
notes: Area 1: the learned method detects which devices are active from the received multi-antenna signal in an IRS-aided uplink, and the metrics are false-alarm and missed-detection probabilities (p. 4); no other area fits. Borderline because the recovered quantity is the activity indicator of known signature sequences, not data symbols; the reviewer should confirm. Eligibility passes: deep unfolding with trained parameters and an MLP gate are learned, the work is at the physical layer, the BS has 32 antennas with an IRS, and results are quantitative. Training procedure and data are not described in the paper, so q2 is 0 although Fig. 4 claims generalization (p. 5). The file is the arXiv preprint v2 of 26 Jun 2025 (arXiv:2502.20183v2); the DOI is not printed in the file.
